title: The Evening Brief: Scheffler dominates, Hunt eyes history, Mariota sidelined
dek: Scottie Scheffler closed out his first win since January with an eight-shot victory at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, Amy Hunt chases a fourth gold medal in Sunday's mixed relay at the European Athletics Championships, and Marcus Mariota's sprained MCL sidelines the Commanders' backup quarterback for the preseason.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Scheffler finally converted a strong tournament position into a dominant victory, ending a seven-month winless stretch and securing the FedEx Cup's No. 1 seed with $23 million in bonus money.
bottom_line: Scheffler's eight-shot victory at St. Jude ended a seven-month winless streak and secured him the FedEx Cup's No. 1 seed with substantial bonus money, while Hunt's three golds put her one race from becoming the first athlete ever to claim four at a single European Championships. Mariota's preseason loss on a noncontact injury leaves Washington thin at backup quarterback as the regular season approaches. Sunday brings Hunt's mixed relay at approximately 20:35 BST, while Makhachev's title defense against undefeated Machado Garry arrives Saturday in Philadelphia.
body: Sunday brought three separate storylines to concrete conclusions across golf, track, and football, while setting up one more championship moment in Brussels.

Scottie Scheffler closed with a 4-under 66 to win the FedEx St. Jude Championship by eight shots, the largest margin in the tournament's 68-year history at TPC Southwind, according to ESPN. Scheffler finished at 17-under 263, with Si Woo Kim in second place at 9-under and Sam Burns and Alex Noren tied for third. The victory marks Scheffler's first win since January, ending a stretch in which he recorded five runner-up finishes and five other top-4 placements. The win clinches him the No. 1 seed through next week's BMW Championship and an additional $23 million in bonus money from the FedEx Cup standings.

At the European Athletics Championships in Brussels, Amy Hunt won her third gold medal Saturday in the women's 4x100m relay and will chase a historic fourth title Sunday in the mixed 4x100m relay. If Hunt wins on Sunday, she will become the first athlete in the event's 92-year history to claim four gold medals at a single edition of the championships. Her three golds came in the 100m, 200m, and women's relay within six days of competition. Great Britain's women's relay team won in 42.05 seconds, finishing more than a second clear of Switzerland. Dina Asher-Smith, 30, matched the championship gold record of seven titles while equalling Irena Szewinska's overall 10-medal record at the championships.

In the NFL, Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL during Friday's preseason opener against the Miami Dolphins and will miss the remainder of the preseason, according to ESPN. The Commanders' backup quarterback left the game after just four plays on a noncontact injury. He handed the ball off to Kaytron Allen before falling to the ground, then walked off under his own power. Washington will proceed through the final weeks of preseason with Jayden Daniels as the only immediately available starter at the position.

Elsewhere, Cameroon claimed their first Women's Africa Cup of Nations title with a 3-0 victory over Malawi in the final at Moulay Hassan Stadium in Rabat. Marie Ngah Manga scored twice and Naomi Eto added one goal in the dominant performance. The victory ended Cameroon's pursuit after three previous final losses, all to Nigeria in 2004, 2014, and 2016. Jacob van Rooyen received a three-match suspension for a swinging arm strike that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir during Saturday night's AFL match, removing the 23-year-old Melbourne forward from next week's match against Western Bulldogs and the Demons' first two finals. Islam Makhachev will defend his welterweight title against Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 in Philadelphia on Saturday, August 16, chasing his 17th consecutive victory, one shy of Anderson Silva's UFC record.
